HIGH YIELD — Memory line
- **Benign ladder** → observation → injection → simple curettage → extended curettage → en bloc resection (Handbook)
- **Malignant** → chemotherapy → **wide resection** → reconstruction → chemotherapy (Prof Abosena)

3.02.b:
### The benign ladder by grade
- Order → **conservative → minimally invasive → curettage**; curettage is the last resort (Handbook)

| Grade (Enneking stage) | Procedure | Example |
|---|---|---|
| **Benign latent** (1) | Observation; simple curettage if needed | Non-ossifying fibroma |
| **Benign active** (2) | Simple curettage  + high-speed burr | Aneurysmal bone cyst |
| **Benign aggressive** (3) | Extended curettage **or** en bloc resection | Giant cell tumour |

- OKU (Orthopaedic Knowledge Update) → the **diagnosis** decides, not the stage · curettage → more recurrence, **better function** than resection

### Latent lesions
- Asymptomatic → **observation** · symptomatic → **non-steroidal anti-inflammatory drugs (NSAIDs) first line** (Handbook)
- Osteoid osteoma → prostaglandin E2 → NSAIDs relieve pain; heals on NSAIDs in **3–4 years** (Campbell) · no NSAID response → question the diagnosis

### Minimally invasive procedures
- **Second line** → when the lesion resists NSAIDs or observation (Handbook)

| Lesion | Procedure | Key points |
|---|---|---|
| **Simple bone cyst** | Aspiration + **methylprednisolone** or bone marrow | 80–200 mg, repeat at 2 months; marrow beat steroid in a trial (OKU Tumors 4) |
| **Osteoid osteoma** (outside the spine) | CT-guided **radiofrequency ablation** (RFA) | **90 °C for 6 minutes**, outpatient; cure 91–95% (Campbell) |
| Aneurysmal bone cyst | Doxycycline sclerotherapy, embolisation | Many sessions; not standard |

- Simple bone cyst → **3 failed injections** → curettage and graft (Campbell)
- RFA near the cord, a nerve root or the neurovascular bundle → **contraindicated** (Miller) · hand, foot, subcutaneous tibia → skin necrosis risk

PITFALL — steroid injection: >90% or failure?
- Campbell → >90% success · OKU → 23–76% failure, marrow beat steroid. Say → "**aspiration and injection first; curettage and graft after three failures**"

- Tibial osteoid osteoma, 13-year-old: film, CT, RFA probe (OKU Tumors 4)

| Site | Centralization | Behavior | Margins | Cortical reaction | Special signs | Verdict |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| diaphyseal | cortical | osteosclerotic | well-defined | intact (thickened) | nidus on computed tomography (CT) | **benign latent** |

- CT-guided RFA of a scapular osteoid osteoma in a child (OKU Tumors 4)
- Humeral simple bone cyst with fracture, 8-year-old: injected, healed at 1 year (Campbell)

| Site | Centralization | Behavior | Margins | Cortical reaction | Special signs | Verdict |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| metaphyseal + diaphyseal | central | osteolytic | well-defined | thinning + pathological fracture | none | **benign latent** |

### Curettage technique

| Curettage type | Technique |
|---|---|
| Simple | Window + curettes  + burr to normal bone + irrigation |
| **Extended** | Simple + **adjuvant** |
| Excisional | Curettage + excision of the soft-tissue extension |
| Curopsy | 2-cm hole, blind scraping → simple bone cyst, ganglion, infection; **never giant cell tumour (GCT) or aneurysmal bone cyst (ABC)** (Prof Abosena) |

- **Window** → as long as the lesion, elliptical along the bone; smaller → tumour left "under the near cortex" (Operative Techniques)
- **High-speed burr** + lavage after hand curettes → only microscopic disease left · **no burr → do not operate** (Prof Abosena)
- Approach **through the muscle**, drain in line · **no Hohmann retractors** → one removable track · walls **sanded, white**; recurrence comes from the **corners** (Prof Abosena)

CLINICAL PEARL — the window's shape
- A hole loses strength when it gets **wider**, not longer → oblong window with **rounded ends** (Operative Techniques)

- Large cortical window, curettage and high-speed burr (Operative Techniques)

### Fillers

| Filler | Gain | Drawback |
|---|---|---|
| **Cement (PMMA)** | Filler **+ thermal adjuvant**; immediate stability; rapid setting; recurrence seen early | Possible subchondral damage |
| Autograft | Fastest; osteogenic + inductive + conductive | Donor morbidity, small amount |
| Cancellous allograft | Plentiful | Only osteoconductive |
| Substitutes | Osteoconductive | Infection (Prof Abosena) |

- Recurrence → **expanding lucency** at the cement edge · thin subchondral bone → **graft layer first**, cement over it · cement never removed
- GCT → graft had **twice** the recurrence of cement (OKU Tumors 4)

- Distal femoral GCT: window, burr, argon beam, screws, cement (Campbell)
- Proximal tibial GCT: graft, cement and locking plate (paper, CC BY-NC)
- Recurrence beside the cement mantle, 2 years after curettage (paper, CC BY)

### Prophylactic fixation
- **Lower limb** → typically required · upper limb → by lesion size versus bone diameter (Handbook) · OKU → **no formula** (OKU Tumors 4)
- Rule of thumb → >3 (or 2½) cortices · window wider than ⅔ · lesion >5–6 cm · crack during curettage (Prof Abosena)
- Construct → plate on the mother bone, screws into soft cement

- Curettage cavities with cement and rods or plates, six sites (Operative Techniques)

### Aggressive lesions — extended curettage and adjuvants
- **Extended curettage** = burr + **adjuvant** → marginal necrosis → margin = **marginal** (Handbook) · cement is filler and adjuvant

| Adjuvant | Depth of necrosis | Risk |
|---|---|---|
| **Phenol** | **<1 mm** (Campbell) | Toxic if spilled |
| Hydrogen peroxide · ethanol | In vitro kill only | Clinical effect uncertain |
| **Argon beam** | ≈4 mm (OKU Tumors 4) | Post-op fracture |
| **Cement (PMMA)** | Up to **6 mm** (OKU Tumors 4) | Small bolus not hot enough |
| **Liquid nitrogen** | **12–14 mm**, the deepest (OKU Tumors 4) | Fracture, skin necrosis, nerve injury |

- Liquid nitrogen → −196 °C, **two** freeze–thaw cycles; prevent fracture by **fixation + cement** (Operative Techniques)
- No adjuvant proven better → burr matters most; GCT recurrence ≈20% with or without (OKU Tumors 4)

PITFALL — adjuvant depth
- Handbook → liquid nitrogen "up to 2 cm" · OKU → 12–14 mm. Say → "**phenol <1 mm, argon ≈4 mm, cement ≈6 mm, liquid nitrogen 1–2 cm**"

- Cryosurgery: direct pour of liquid nitrogen with soft tissues padded (Operative Techniques)
- Argon-probe cryoablation of a proximal tibial GCT (Operative Techniques)
- Fracture after cryoablation and bone graft alone, then endoprosthesis (Operative Techniques)
- Skin burn from spilled liquid nitrogen (Operative Techniques)

### En bloc resection
- **Second option** for aggressive lesions → mass + wall + reactive zone + normal cuff, compartment intact → margin = **wide** (Handbook)
- Grade 3 or recurrent GCT · expendable bones (proximal fibula, distal ulna, clavicle) → no reconstruction

EXAM PEARL — curettage versus en bloc
- GCT recurrence → curettage alone **42%** · + adjuvant + filler **19%** · wide resection **7.7%** (OKU Tumors 4)

3.03.b:
### The four margins
- Margin = dissection plane versus the **pseudocapsule** (reactive zone) → foci inside it = **satellites**, beyond it in the compartment = **skip metastases**

| Margin | Plane | Left behind | Recurrence (malignant) | Use |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| **Intralesional** | Inside the tumour | Gross tumour | **100%** (Miller) | Benign curettage; palliation |
| **Marginal** | Through the pseudocapsule | Satellites | **25–50%** (Miller) | Encapsulated benign (lipoma) |
| **Wide** | Normal tissue all round | Skip lesions | **<10%** (Miller) | **Sarcomas** |
| **Radical** | Whole compartment | Nothing | Lowest | Rarely needed now |

- Four margins drawn on bone and on soft-tissue sarcoma (Prof Abosena)
- Excision types for soft-tissue and bone sarcoma (Operative Techniques)

- **Amputation** is not a fifth margin → resection or amputation × 4 margins = **8 procedures** (Campbell)
- **Quality beats quantity** → a thin fascial layer beats a thick fatty one

- Enneking classification of amputations (Campbell)

PITFALL — how wide is wide?
- Prof Abosena → "2–3 cm, not less" · OKU → 3 cm traditional, **1.5 cm** acceptable · Campbell → no fixed distance. Say → "**bone cut 2–3 cm beyond the magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) extent, normal cuff all round**"

| Margin needed | Tumours |
|---|---|
| Intralesional | Benign latent, active; aggressive with adjuvant; palliation of metastasis |
| Intralesional allowed | Grade I central chondrosarcoma of a limb → recurrence equal to wide (OKU Tumors 4) |
| Wide | High-grade sarcoma; parosteal osteosarcoma; adamantinoma; chordoma |
| Wide (curative) | Solitary metastasis, good prognosis (renal, breast) |

PITFALL — extended curettage: marginal or intralesional?
- Handbook → extended curettage = **marginal** (the wall is removed by necrosis) · Campbell, Enneking → every curettage, simple or extended, is **intralesional**: the plane passes through the tumour; the adjuvant only extends the cell kill (Campbell p882, 952)
- Say → "extended curettage: intralesional in Enneking's terms; the Handbook calls it marginal because the adjuvant kills the wall."

- ≥90% necrosis + wider margin → least recurrence (OKU Tumors 4)

3.04.b:
### Surgical management
- 90–95% of sarcomas → limb-sparing surgery (Operative Techniques) · surgery alone cures **15–20%** of osteosarcoma → micrometastases in ≈80% (Campbell)

### Systemic therapy
- Three arms → **radiotherapy** (radiosensitive tumours, metastatic pain) · **chemotherapy** (chemosensitive) · **hormonal** (breast, prostate; radioiodine for thyroid) (Handbook)
- Bisphosphonates, denosumab → fewer skeletal events → 11 Myeloma & metastasis · pain → NSAIDs → morphine → blocks → physio and psychotherapy (Handbook)

### Tumour-specific treatment

| Modality | Tumours |
|---|---|
| **Resection only** | Conventional chondrosarcoma · parosteal and low-grade central osteosarcoma · adamantinoma · clear-cell chondrosarcoma |
| **Resection + chemotherapy** | Conventional osteosarcoma · mesenchymal, dedifferentiated chondrosarcoma · high-grade fibrosarcoma, undifferentiated pleomorphic sarcoma of bone |
| **Resection + radiotherapy** | Chordoma with a margin that is not wide · most soft-tissue sarcomas |
| **Chemotherapy + resection ± radiotherapy** | **Ewing sarcoma** · rhabdomyosarcoma |
| **Chemotherapy + radiotherapy only** | Myeloma · leukaemia · lymphoma → surgery only for fracture |

- Periosteal osteosarcoma → chemotherapy **controversial** (OKU Tumors 4)

EXAM PEARL — why Ewing differs
- Ewing is **radiosensitive** → radiotherapy can replace surgery in pelvis or spine; wide resection avoids radiation-induced sarcoma (Campbell)

### Radiotherapy
- Free radicals → deoxyribonucleic acid (DNA) damage; hypoxia protects → 1.5–2 gray (Gy) a day (Campbell)
- **Radiosensitive** → small round cell tumours (Ewing, lymphoma, myeloma), most carcinoma metastases · **radioresistant** → most sarcomas, renal metastases

| Modality | Point |
|---|---|
| **External beam** | Most common; photons, IMRT (intensity-modulated radiotherapy) |
| **Intraoperative** | One electron dose 10–20 Gy on the bed (OKU Tumors 4) |
| **Brachytherapy** | Catheters in the bed, loaded later (iridium-192) |
| Protons · carbon ions | Bragg peak → children, chordoma, unresectable sarcoma |

| Soft-tissue sarcoma | Pre-operative | Post-operative |
|---|---|---|
| Dose · field | **50 Gy**, tumour only | **60–66 Gy**, whole field (OKU Tumors 4) |
| Main problem | **Wound complications 35%** | Wound 17%; **fibrosis, stiffness, fracture** (OKU Tumors 4) |
| Control · survival | Equal | Equal (O'Sullivan trial) |

| Complication | Detail |
|---|---|
| Acute | Erythema → desquamation, hair loss, wound breakdown |
| Late soft tissue | Fibrosis, oedema, stiffness, **muscle wasting**, pigmentation |
| Bone | **Fracture** 6% (OKU Tumors 4), osteonecrosis |
| Child | **Physeal arrest** even after 20 Gy (OKU Tumors 4), scoliosis, limb-length discrepancy |
| **Radiation-induced sarcoma** | Criteria below |

- Radiation osteonecrosis of the femoral head after breast-metastasis radiotherapy (Campbell)
- Bone-in-bone vertebrae after childhood radiotherapy (Campbell)

### Radiation-induced sarcoma
- Criteria → Cahan (1948), minor revisions since; **all four** must be met (OKU Tumors 4; Greenspan)
1) **Irradiated site** → previous radiotherapy there, usually ≥3,000 rads within 4 weeks; reported after only 800 rads (Greenspan; OKU Tumors 4)
2) **Inside the field** → the sarcoma arises within the radiation field (OKU Tumors 4; Greenspan)
3) **Latent period ≥3 years** → average 11 years, range 4–40 (Greenspan; OKU Tumors 4)
4) **Different histology** → not the same type as the original (benign or malignant) lesion that was irradiated (OKU Tumors 4; Greenspan)

- Usually **osteosarcoma**, also fibrosarcoma, undifferentiated pleomorphic sarcoma · rate ≈**1%** after >2500 centigray (cGy), usually **10–15 years** later (Campbell)
- Flat bones (skull, spine, clavicle, ribs, scapula, pelvis) · major concern in **children** · prognosis poor → 9 Osteosarcoma

PITFALL — "children, pelvis most common"
- Handbook → "in children", "pelvis most common" · OKU → commoner in **women**; Campbell → no single site. Say → "**four criteria: irradiated site, inside the field, latent period ≥3 years, different histology; usually osteosarcoma**"

- Radiation-induced sarcoma of the ilium, 63-year-old, radium 15 years earlier: film and CT (Greenspan)

| Site | Centralization | Behavior | Margins | Cortical reaction | Special signs | Verdict |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| ilium | — | osteolytic | ill-defined | destruction + soft-tissue mass | none | **malignant** |

### Chemotherapy
- **Adjuvant** → after surgery · **neoadjuvant** → before, introduced by **Rosen** · osteosarcoma and Ewing → **chemo → surgery → chemo** (Prof Abosena)
- Neoadjuvant benefits → **micrometastases** treated at once · **shrinks** tumour and vascularity · drugs tested **in vivo** (necrosis = prognosis) · **time** to make the prosthesis (Handbook)
- **Good response** → necrosis **>90%** (OKU Tumors 4) · timing trial (POG-8651, Pediatric Oncology Group) → **no survival difference**

PITFALL — poor responder: change the drugs?
- Prof Abosena → change drugs below 90–95% · OKU (EURAMOS-1, European and American Osteosarcoma Study) → no survival gain. Say → "**necrosis is prognostic; changing drugs has not improved survival**"

| Agent | Specific complication |
|---|---|
| Regimens | Osteosarcoma **MAP** (methotrexate, doxorubicin, cisplatin) · Ewing **VDC/IE** (vincristine, doxorubicin, cyclophosphamide / ifosfamide, etoposide) |
| **Doxorubicin** | **Cardiotoxic** above **500 mg/m²**; dexrazoxane protects (OKU Tumors 4) |
| **Cisplatin** | **Nephrotoxic + ototoxic** above **360 mg/m²** (OKU Tumors 4) |
| **Methotrexate** | Mucositis, renal, liver → **leucovorin** rescue |
| **Vincristine** | **Neurotoxic** |
| **Cyclophosphamide · ifosfamide** | **Haemorrhagic cystitis**, **bladder cancer**, infertility |
| Etoposide · cyclophosphamide | **Secondary leukaemia** 1–2% (OKU Tumors 4) |

- Children → **growth arrest**, transient (OKU Tumors 4) · bone → fracture risk
- Chemo-resistant → conventional chondrosarcoma, chordoma, adamantinoma, parosteal osteosarcoma

HIGH YIELD — drug and organ (memory aid)
- **D**oxorubicin → **heart** · **C**isplatin → **ear + kidney** · **V**incristine → **nerve** · **C**yclophosphamide → **bladder**
